featured_reviews.name: Sanika Ajgaonkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Munchbox Thali — a newly opened Rajasthani thali spot — is a bright, cozy addition to the city’s thali scene. From the moment we walked in, the vibrant decor and comfy sofa seating made us feel like settling in for a long, happy meal. 🛋️🌈
We tried the Summer Special Thali and loved how homely it felt. The Aam Ras was silky and refreshingly sweet — perfect between bites. 🥭 The Mal Poha was light and fluffy with just the right hint of spice. 🍚
Highlights? Definitely the Gujarati Kadhi, Dahi Vada, and Khaman. The Kadhi had a lovely tangy creaminess, the Dahi Vada was soft and seasoned well, and the Khaman simply melted in the mouth. 😍 For those who like heat, the Chinese Samosa is a playful, spicy Indo-Chinese twist — crispy outside, saucy and punchy inside. 🥟🌶️
Staff here are genuinely friendly and keep checking in — they’ll happily top up your plate until you’re full. That level of warmth makes the whole experience feel like eating at a friend’s place. 🤗
For bloggers and creators: the colorful interiors and sofa seating are great for photos and reels. 📸 Daylight brings out the decor’s pop of color, so aim for an afternoon visit. The food leans homestyle rather than experimental, which is great if you want crowd-pleasing, comforting content. Portions are generous and prices feel fair for what you get.

featured_reviews.review_text: Ambience is nice, food is good and tasty, a little sweeter. But very competitive as compared to Maharaja Bhog. featured_reviews.name: Suyog Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited The Munchbox Thali (at the location where 5 Spice used to be), and it turned out to be quite a wholesome experience.
At around ₹600, the thali is incredibly elaborate and served in beautiful brass plates and bowls, which immediately adds a royal touch. The spread includes 2 farsan (we had dhokla and tikki), 4 vegetables (including a paneer dish, a seasonal preparation, a potato curry, and a sprout-based dish), along with 2 types of rotis and puris. On top of that, you get 2 dals, kadhi, and 3 varieties of rice including khichdi. There’s also a salad, 3–4 types of chutneys, a chaat item, and 2 desserts — for us, it was seasonal Hapus aamras and moong dal halwa. And yes, expect generous use of ghee in almost everything.
Valet parking is available, which is definitely a big plus given the busy Borivali area.
Be prepared for a wait — 99% of the time there’s a queue, though they’ve thoughtfully arranged ample seating downstairs. The dining hall is on the first floor and can accommodate around 75–80 people comfortably.
A thoughtful addition is a single-person seating lift, making it convenient for elderly guests to access the dining area on the first floor.
The ambience is a standout — it genuinely gives you vibes of royal palaces from Udaipur or Jaipur, making the experience feel special rather than just another meal outing.
Service deserves a special mention — the staff is warm, attentive, and serve with genuine care and enthusiasm.
Coming to the food, everything felt fresh and had a homely touch. The flavors were balanced — not overly spicy or greasy. While the potato curry and a couple of vegetable dishes could have been better, the rest of the spread was quite satisfying.
Overall, a great place for a hearty, traditional Gujarati–Rajasthani thali experience with a royal ambience. Worth the wait if you’re in the mood to indulge!

featured_reviews.name: JINESH G PAREKH
featured_reviews.review_text:
The ambience was really good and gives a pleasant dining experience. However, the food was average overall, and the Jain food in particular was not up to the mark in terms of taste.

I tried three Jain sabjis Green Gujarati, Paneer, and Kathol. Frankly, all three were below average in taste. Those who specifically prefer Jain food should avoid this place. Paneer tastes like it was fake paneer. Worst it was .

There was no taste in anything be it roti, dhokla, sweets, or even the mango ras, which was extremely watery and tasteless.

The service is extremely fast almost too fast. Dishes are served in quick succession, leaving very little time to decide what to eat and what to skip, which unfortunately leads to a lot of food wastage.

At the time of entry, there were quite a few unnecessary questions (like number of people, arrival timing, etc.), even though it wasn’t very crowded being a working day.

What stood out the most was that the management seemed more focused on seat turnover , how quickly customers can sit, eat, and leave so the next set can occupy the same table, rather than ensuring customer satisfaction, especially in terms of food quality and taste.

It’s okay for a one-time experience, but for repeat visits, I would highly recommend Maharaja Bhog. It is slightly more expensive but definitely worth it for the overall quality and dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Aaditya Chaturvedi
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am really really happy with the service which we got at The Munchbox Thali. We booked 2 tables for 8, and we ordered Jain Thali. The food was Jain friendly, that is, no onion and no garlic, although some restaurants fail to prepare it correctly.

Best items which I loved in the thali were: aamras, chhaas, paneer, and dal, and all the other items were great too.

The servers were really polite and not even waiting for us to actually call them. They were always at their toes to serve us. 100% recommended for family dine-ins, and a great family outing.

featured_reviews.name: Derrick D'Souza
featured_reviews.review_text:
After my wife's inability to cook due to orthopaedic issues, I was scanning the mobile for some outside caterer to fill in the void. And my eyes happened to see the food app " Tiffinkart " which instaneously caught my attention. I was not on the wrong track when I made my choice and both of us, decided to try out this catering avenue.
I got in touch with Mrs Sharmila and after a brief discussion about the rates and menu to go with, hit on her Tiffinkart app to get her to deliver food for us at our residence.
On the very first day of receiving her tiffin (one veg, the other non veg) we were delighted to see such mouth watering fare, vis-a-vis the price attached to it. oHer food is very tasty, and delicious and easily digestable. This Lady is very accommodating, kind, gentle and understanding towards the need of the hour.
However, my interaction with her made me feel like she is a family member. This is an added quality to the food she serves. No wonder a clientele stretches from Churchgate to Virar as far as I know.
Its amazing how this young, charming lady can meet the needs of those in need of good food to feed themselves.
My to all is that I have tried, tested and am still enjoying the meals coming from her gracious kitchen.

featured_reviews.name: Amit Arekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently tried Tiffinkart and was wowed by the quality of their food. Both the veg and non-veg options were flavorful and perfectly prepared. Each dish reflected great care and quality, arriving at the perfect temperature.

A special thanks to Shreeya, the owner, whose proactive approach added to the wonderful experience. Her attention to service and detail truly stands out, ensuring everything was just right.

For anyone seeking delicious and reliable meals, Tiffinkart is a fantastic choice. I highly recommend them for their exceptional food and service.
